key_insight: MARTINI-3 coarse-grained clay parameters can capture how phyllosilicate surface polarity and organoclay modification control polymer-blend compatibilization and interfacial structure.
engineering_relevance: These transferable parameters enable faster multiscale design of polymer-clay nanocomposites and help predict when clays will reduce immiscible polymer interfacial tension.
method: Derived clay interaction parameters from hydration free energies using Lifshitz theory and experimental surface tension data.
Refined the coarse-grained model against all-atom MD of thermoplastic starch–clay composites across structural, thermodynamic, and dynamic metrics.
Applied the validated model to large-scale TPS–PE blend simulations with C12TAB-modified montmorillonite to probe interphase compatibilization.
evidence_signal: The model reproduced radial distribution functions, two-body excess entropy, and interfacial tension trends, including a TPS–PE reduction from 45 mN/m to 13.06 mN/m.
watch_item: Transferability may depend on clay chemistry, organic modifier type, and blend composition, so new systems still need validation before use.
paper_title: Characterization and Quantification of Immiscible Polymer Blend Compatibilization by Phyllosilicate Clays
